question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $90u+39v=\text{gcd}(90,39).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}90 & = & 39\cdot 2 & + & 12 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 39 & = & 12\cdot 3 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 12 & = & 3\cdot 4 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(90,39)=3.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =90-39\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =39-12\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =39-12\cdot 3 \\  & =39-[90-39\cdot 2]\cdot 3 \\  & =39\cdot 7-90\cdot 3 \\  & =90\cdot (-3)+39\cdot 7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-3)+7=4.
$$
